title: Escape Velocity

references.label: NCERT Physics Part I, Class 11 — Gravitation

explanation: Escape velocity is the minimum speed needed at a planet's surface for an object to permanently escape its gravitational pull, found by setting total mechanical energy (KE + gravitational PE) at the surface equal to zero (just enough energy to reach infinity with zero leftover speed). It depends only on the planet's mass M and radius R (or equivalently its surface gravity g and R), NOT on the mass of the escaping object or its launch direction (ignoring atmospheric drag).
commonMistakes: Assuming escape velocity depends on the mass of the escaping object — it cancels out entirely in the derivation and is independent of the escaping mass.
Confusing escape velocity with orbital velocity — orbital velocity at the same radius is always ve/√2, noticeably smaller.
genZNote: 11.2 km/s: Earth's official 'you may now leave' speed.
